issues.legal_issue: A dispute between parties to a decree that an execution sale exceeded the decree must be raised through execution proceedings rather than a separate suit.
material_facts: The decree directed sale of mortgage rights, but the execution sale included the underlying properties.
The persons challenging the sale were parties to the decree.
The challenge was brought as a separate suit seeking relief from the sale.
issues.conclusion: The claim that the sale exceeded the decree was barred as a separate suit by section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure and could be pursued only by an application in execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, disputes between parties to a decree concerning the execution, discharge or satisfaction of the decree must be determined by the executing court, not by a separate suit. The Court relied on and approved J. Marret v. Md. K. Shirazi & Sons, Venkatachalapathy Aiyen v. Perumal Aiyen, Biru Mahata v. Shyama Charan Khawas, Abdul Karim v. Islamunnissa Bibi, and Lakshminarayan v. Laduram.

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: The proceeding challenges a sale carried out in execution of a decree.
predicates.parties_to_decree: The persons disputing the execution sale were parties to the decree.
predicates.sale_exceeded_decree: The execution sale covered property or rights beyond what the decree authorised.

issues.definition: When parties to a decree challenge an execution sale as exceeding the decree, the challenge must be pursued in execution proceedings.

issues.legal_issue: A suit raising a matter reserved to execution proceedings may be treated as an execution application, subject to limitation and jurisdiction.
material_facts: The plaint sought relief concerning an execution sale alleged to exceed the decree.
The suit was filed in a court that had jurisdiction over the properties, although the decree had been passed by another court.
The plaint was filed within the limitation period measured from dispossession.
issues.conclusion: Under section 47(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the plaint could be treated as an execution application, subject to objections concerning limitation or jurisdiction; the Court directed that it be so treated.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers a court, subject to objections as to limitation or jurisdiction, to treat a suit as a proceeding under section 47. The Court applied this provision after finding that limitation did not bar the application and that the jurisdiction objection had been waived.

rule.if: separate_suit_about_execution and relief_belongs_in_execution_proceedings and limitation_does_not_bar_application and jurisdiction_objection_is_unavailable

predicates.separate_suit_about_execution: A party brought a separate suit seeking relief about an act done in executing a decree.
predicates.relief_belongs_in_execution_proceedings: The relief sought is one that must be determined in proceedings executing the decree.
predicates.limitation_does_not_bar_application: The application for the relief would not be barred by limitation when the suit was filed.
predicates.jurisdiction_objection_is_unavailable: No effective objection prevents the court from entertaining the matter as an execution application.

issues.definition: A suit seeking relief that belongs in execution proceedings may be treated as an execution application when limitation does not bar it and no effective jurisdiction objection prevents that treatment.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for relief from a void execution sale is governed by the general limitation article, with time running from dispossession rather than from the sale.
material_facts: The decree authorised sale of mortgage rights, not the underlying properties, so the sale of those properties was found to be void.
The applicants were parties to the suit in which the decree was passed and sought recovery of properties taken under the sale.
The plaint was filed within three years of the relevant dispossession.
issues.conclusion: Articles 165 and 166 of the Indian Limitation Act did not govern the claim; article 181 applied, and time ran from dispossession, making the plaint timely when treated as an execution application.
issues.legal_principle: Article 165 applies to applications for restoration by persons other than judgment-debtors, not to a judgment-debtor's claim that property was wrongly taken in execution. Article 166 applies to setting aside a voidable sale, not to a sale that is void and has no legal existence. Article 181 governs an application for relief from a void sale, and limitation begins when the purchaser interferes with possession or dispossesses the claimant. The Court relied on Vachali Rohini v. Kombi Aliassan, Rasul v. Amina, Bahir Das v. Girish Chandra, Seshagiri Rao v. Srinivasa Rao, Rajagopalier v. Ramanujachariar, Manmothanath Ghose v. Lachmi Devi, Nirode Kali Roy v. Harendra Nath, Ma We Gyan v. Maung Than Byu, and Chengalraya v. Kollapuri.

rule.if: execution_sale_challenge and claimant_is_party_to_decree and sale_is_void and claimant_was_dispossessed

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: The proceeding seeks relief concerning a sale carried out in execution of a decree.
predicates.claimant_is_party_to_decree: The person seeking relief was a party to the suit in which the decree was made.
predicates.sale_is_void: The execution sale was unauthorised by the decree and therefore had no legal effect.
predicates.claimant_was_dispossessed: The purchaser under the sale took possession of, or interfered with the claimant's possession of, the property.

issues.definition: For a party to a decree seeking relief from a void execution sale, limitation runs from the purchaser's dispossession or interference with possession, not from the sale.

issues.legal_issue: A court that acquires jurisdiction over property after its transfer may have inherent jurisdiction to entertain execution proceedings, and an objection to an irregular assumption of that jurisdiction may be waived if not raised at the earliest opportunity.
material_facts: The property had been transferred to the jurisdiction of the court in which the suit was filed.
The decree had been passed by a different court and had not been formally transferred for execution.
The appellant did not object to the court's jurisdiction in the written statement or at the earliest opportunity.
issues.conclusion: The court entertaining the application had, at least, inherent jurisdiction over the property; any assumption of execution jurisdiction was irregular rather than wholly without jurisdiction, and the objection was waived because it was not raised at the earliest opportunity.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 37 and 38 of the Code of Civil Procedure govern which court may execute a decree. The Court did not decide the general conflict over whether a court to which the subject matter has been transferred can execute the decree without a formal transfer. It applied Balakrishnayya v. Linga Rao: transfer of the subject matter gives the receiving court inherent jurisdiction, and an irregular assumption of jurisdiction is waivable if no objection is made at the earliest opportunity.

predicates.execution_application_in_transferee_cour: An application to execute a decree is made in a court other than the court that passed the decree.
predicates.property_transferred_into_court_jurisdic: The property covered by the decree has come within the jurisdiction of the court receiving the application.
predicates.no_objection_at_earliest_opportunity: The opposing party did not object to that court's jurisdiction at the earliest opportunity.

issues.definition: When execution is sought in a court whose jurisdiction includes transferred property, a party who fails to object at the earliest opportunity waives an objection to an irregular assumption of jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A court may permit a pure question of law requiring no further factual investigation to be raised for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The objection that the suit was barred by section 47 had not been raised in the written statement and was advanced at the second-appeal stage.
The issue required no further investigation of facts and had been argued as a question of law.
The allegations in the plaint concerning the issue were obscure enough that the appellant might have missed their import.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was permitted to raise the section 47 objection because it was a pure question of law requiring no further factual investigation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its discretion to permit a new legal contention on appeal where it required no further investigation of facts and had been understood and debated as a question of law. The judgment does not cite a specific statutory provision or earlier case for this procedural ruling.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal in which a party seeks to advance a contention not raised earlier.
predicates.new_contention_is_pure_question_of_law: The new contention can be decided as a question of law on the existing record.
predicates.no_further_fact_investigation_required: Deciding the contention requires no further investigation of facts.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, a court may permit a new contention when it is a legal issue that can be decided without further factual investigation.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who obtains relief from a void execution sale may be denied mesne profits for the period before the court's decision when the claimant's gross negligence caused the difficulties.
material_facts: The respondents did not appear in the original suit to assert their rights.
When they intervened during execution, they mainly relied on an allegation of fraud that was later rejected.
They did not press the successful excessive-execution argument until the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were denied mesne profits up to the date of the Court's decision but were entitled to their share of the net income from that date until they were put in separate possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its discretion over the monetary relief accompanying the order, taking account of the respondents' gross negligence at all stages. The judgment cites no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this adjustment.

predicates.claimant_seeks_monetary_property_profits: A claimant who obtains relief concerning property also seeks profits attributable to that property.
predicates.claimant_grossly_negligent_in_asserting_: The claimant repeatedly failed to assert the relevant property rights in a timely and effective manner.

issues.definition: When a property claimant seeks profits and was grossly negligent in asserting the relevant rights, the court may deny profits for the period before its decision.
